newsitem.title: USA: McVeigh accuses FBI in Waco deaths.
newsitem.headline: McVeigh accuses FBI in Waco deaths.

text.p: A letter in which Oklahoma City bombing suspect Timothy McVeigh accused federal agents of murdering children at the Branch Davidian compound in Waco, Texas, was handed over to the FBI on Wednesday.

Phil Bacharach, the Oklahoma Gazette reporter who received McVeigh's letter, said FBI agents asked for the original after excerpts were published in the weekly newspaper on Wednesday. He said he turned over the letter voluntarily.
Bacharach said the agent who collected the letter "put on rubber gloves, placed it inside a bag, sealed it, thanked me and left" without explaining what the FBI wanted it for.
In the two-page handwritten letter, McVeigh alleged that FBI agents murdered the Branch Davidians and covered up the truth of what happened when the Waco compound went up in flames on April 19, 1993.

"The public never saw the Davidians' home video of their cute babies, adorable children, loving mothers or protective fathers," McVeigh said in the letter, excerpts of which were published in the Oklahoma Gazette.

"Nor did they see pictures of the charred remains of children's bodies. Therefore, they didn't care when these families died a slow, torturous death as they were gassed and burned alive at the hands of the FBI," he said.
Calling the FBI "wizards of propaganda," McVeigh, 28, drew a parallel between the Waco deaths and his own imprisonment.

"The idea is that once the FBI can control the flow of information, they can then determine their target. In my case, I have been sealed away in federal prison and denied most visitation and free communication," he said.
"People need to question and analyse what they hear, and ponder the motivations of those spreading the propaganda."
Branch Davidian cult leader David Koresh and at least 80 of his followers were killed by flames or gunfire when the FBI raided their compound at the end of a 51-day siege.
Federal officials say cult members started the fire themselves but anti-government groups blame the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms.

Prosecutors in the trial of McVeigh, which began last week, allege that he blew up the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in downtown Oklahoma City on the second anniversary of the Branch Davidian fire as an act of revenge against the federal government.
The blast killed 168 people, including 19 children.
Bacharach said he was surprised by the level of media -- and FBI -- interest in the letter which he received last November but only published on Wednesday.

"It didn't strike us as a breakthrough," Bacharach told Reuters. "We were surprised because McVeigh's interest, or level of passion, over Waco has been so well publicised and documented over the last two years."
McVeigh's attorney, Stephen Jones, confirmed that McVeigh's letter was legitimate but said it had no relevance to the bombing case.
The slow process of jury selection for McVeigh's trial continued on Wednesday in Denver, where the case was moved from Oklahoma to guarantee him a fair hearing.
